prize_parts.citation: for introducing firm heterogeneity into trade theory, showing how selection into exporting and reallocation across firms shape the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: one part, B005, with Helpman and Melitz. What changed is how I weigh it against B011 and how narrowly I would word the citation. The case rests on three things. First, Melitz (2003) is a tractable, general model of exporter selection and within-industry reallocation, and it gives a distinct channel for gains from trade. Second, the framework has been confronted with firm-level and transaction-level data in many countries for more than twenty years. The selection and reallocation margins it predicts are observable in micro data. That is the kind of confirmation I know best from my own work on pricing, invoicing and pass-through. Third, the credit is separable. Helpman's contribution here is the firm-level extension work, namely the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple analysis of exports versus foreign direct investment and the Helpman-Melitz-Rubinstein work on estimating trade flows with firm selection and zero trade flows. It does not depend on the monopolistic-competition base that the 2008 prize covered, and it does not depend on his protection-for-sale work (B020). I answer the chair's wording question as follows. The citation should honour the theoretical integration of firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory. It should not claim the empirical discovery of exporter premia (Bernard, Jensen and co-authors), the Ricardian Eaton-Kortum strand, or the later quantitative spatial work (Redding). I hold this view on the scientific record alone. The round-1 tallies play no role in it. B011's six preferred-part positions do not move my assessment of merit, and B005's broad ranking support does not move it either.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still attribution. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited, and a two-name citation cannot fully allocate credit in a diffuse literature. Helpman's marginal credit is the contested element. A Melitz-only award would be cleaner on attribution but would leave out the export-versus-FDI organisation-of-firms strand. Krugman's 2008 prize covers the earlier monopolistic-competition framework, so the citation has to stay anchored on selection and reallocation. Some welfare conclusions depend on functional form (Pareto productivity, CES demand). The size of the gains is therefore less robust than the qualitative selection mechanism. I also accept that B011 is a strong rival. It has a clean two-author origin and nearly three decades of use, and the trade case is arguably harder to draft cleanly. A committee that treats trade as adequately recognised in 2008, or that weighs attribution above breadth of empirical confirmation, could reasonably choose B011.

responses.point: Hassler prefers B011 (Kiyotaki and Moore). He says it is the clean originator of the collateral-price feedback, the 2022 prize covers distinct ground, and B005's attribution is harder to draw because of Krugman 2008 and the uncredited empirical-trade contributors. He ranks B005 as his alternative.
responses.response: I accept that B011 is the cleaner attribution and that the 2022 overlap is a wording issue more than a disqualification. I will not oppose a two-name B011 if its citation clearly separates collateral-price feedback from bank-focused and accelerator work. Where we differ is how the two cases are confirmed. For B005 the selection and reallocation margins can be observed directly in firm-level data across many countries. For B011 the quantitative size of the collateral channel is established mainly through modelling and crisis episodes, as several of your supporters concede. I treat that as a difference in the kind of evidence, not a verdict that one is the better discovery. On your Krugman point, I would answer that Helpman's credit comes from the firm-level extensions, and I would make that explicit in the wording.

responses.point: Krusell prefers B011 and lists B005 as his first alternative. He sees the two as close, with B011 ahead on attribution. He notes that Krugman's 2008 prize and the uncredited names make priority on B005 contestable, and he says B005 is where he would go if the 2022 overlap proved decisive.
responses.response: I agree that the two are close, and I share your sense that the ordering turns on attribution and the 2022 overlap, not on scientific quality. I take the priority point seriously. I would say that the Bernard-Jensen facts and the Eaton-Kortum model supplied important inputs and stand apart from the Melitz selection mechanism. The citation can honour the theoretical integration without adjudicating who first documented exporter heterogeneity. If the committee finds that wording insufficient, a Melitz-centred credit is the fallback. I think it is less complete, because it omits the export-versus-FDI strand, but I would rather concede that than widen to a contested group. Your 'about 15 prizes' tournament question is a real consideration, but I do not think breadth of support or concentration of support should settle the choice.

responses.point: Andersson prefers B011 with Kiyotaki and Moore only. He lists B005 as his first alternative and says he could support it if the attribution question were settled convincingly. He argues that the Helpman credit depends on a broader programme that Krugman's prize partly covers.
responses.response: This is the objection I most want to answer, because it decides whether you can move. Helpman's credit in this entry has an identifiable core that is separate from the monopolistic-competition base. It consists of the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple treatment of exporting versus foreign direct investment under firm heterogeneity, and the work on estimating trade flows with selection into partner markets. These sit on the Melitz side of the lineage, not the Krugman side. I do not claim the overlap with 2008 is zero. That is why I would anchor the citation on selection and reallocation across firms and say nothing about love of variety or scale economies. If the committee is not persuaded, the right response is a narrower credit, not dropping the field. I would not dismiss that choice as a matter of taste.

responses.point: Boppart moved to B005 after ranking B001 first. He would word the citation around firm-heterogeneity theory and selection, not the empirical exporter-premia discovery. He keeps B011 as his first alternative and would not oppose it with similar attribution care.
responses.response: We are close, and I agree on the wording: a citation built on the theory of firm heterogeneity and selection, with Redding left out as a later and more specialised extender. I would add one point for the vote. If the committee prefers B011, nothing in your file or mine suggests that B005 should be dropped as an alternative. It could carry later, given its maturity. On B020, I agree with your treatment. Helpman's protection-for-sale work should not be bundled in, and a second part would breach the three-person limit and dilute the achievement.

responses.point: Strömberg prefers B011 but calls B005 the natural alternative. He agrees with its scientific assessment and says he would not oppose it if the committee concluded the credit lines were clean. He holds that Krugman 2008 and the uncredited empirical contributors make priority harder than for B011.
responses.response: I appreciate that, and I do not want to overstate how clean the credit lines are. The recipients can be named cleanly, with Melitz as the model and Helpman as the extender to the firm's organisational choices. The surrounding literature is dispersed. B011 has the advantage of a single originating paper. I would answer that a prize does not need a single paper if the contribution has a recognisable core, which here is selection into exporting and reallocation. I also agree with your remark that breadth of ranking support is a reason to examine a candidate, not a reason to elect it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee finds a selection-and-reallocation citation sufficient to answer the Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum attribution concern, or prefers a Melitz-centred credit.
How much marginal credit Helpman has beyond the lineage covered by Krugman's 2008 prize. I locate it in the firm-level extension work, but others may read the boundary differently.

Whether the 2022 overlap and the indirect identification of the collateral channel weigh against B011 as heavily as I suggest, or whether wording resolves them as its supporters argue. I have not independently verified the empirical literature and rely on general knowledge.
Whether the committee regards trade as adequately recognised by the 2008 prize. That is a judgement about timing and field balance, not about the quality of the science.

The three-person limit prevents a coherent two-part pairing of B005 with a two-name B011 or B034. I therefore support a single part, and I could not find a pairing that avoids weakening one of the attributions.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Helpman, Melitz, Redding or any other credited name on the shortlisted entries is apparent from the supplied profile. I disclose the following public connections, which are not adjudicated. My research field (pricing under imperfect competition, exchange-rate pass-through, invoicing, trade) is adjacent to B005, and I rank my own field's neighbours with that in mind. It is also close to the industrial-organisation candidate B034, my second alternative. I have co-authored with the chair, John Hassler, and with former chair Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026). Hassler prefers B011, a competing configuration, and I have addressed his position on its merits. I am married to Magdalena Andersson, a Swedish politician. This is noted only as a public fact, and I have found no evidence that it bears on my assessment. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
